l4_steps.name: Extract flight schedule & compute GSE demand
l4_steps.input: Inbound/outbound flight schedule, stand allocation plan, aircraft type mix
l4_steps.output: GSE demand matrix by stand, flight, and equipment type
l4_steps.kpi: GSE demand forecast accuracy ≥95% vs actual utilisation
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS schedule feeds lag 2–4 hr behind real-time slot changes; GSE demand mismatches occur at congested airports during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Allocate GSE units to flights via AMS rules
l4_steps.input: GSE demand matrix, current GSE fleet registry with asset status
l4_steps.output: GSE-to-flight assignment schedule published to ramp supervisors
l4_steps.kpi: GSE assignment completion ≥60 min before first departure of each wave; compliance ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual supervisor overrides bypass AMS allocation logic, creating last-minute equipment conflicts during irregular operations and peak waves

l4_steps.name: Confirm GSE serviceability against maintenance roster
l4_steps.input: GSE assignment schedule, open work orders, scheduled maintenance calendar
l4_steps.output: Confirmed serviceable GSE list; pool shortfall flag if serviceability rate below threshold
l4_steps.kpi: GSE fleet serviceability rate ≥92% at start of each operational day
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS maintenance records not always updated in real time by field technicians; apparent serviceability rates overstate actual availability, discovered only at stand

l4_steps.name: Pre-position GSE at assigned stand before block-in
l4_steps.input: Confirmed GSE assignment, inbound ETA from AMS flight information display
l4_steps.output: GSE physically staged at correct stand ≥30 min before block-in
l4_steps.kpi: On-stand pre-positioning compliance ≥95% of turns; late positioning incidents ≤2% per month
l4_steps.pain_point: GPS-based GSE telematics not universally deployed; manual radio check-in introduces positioning errors during peak waves, causing stand conflicts

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-use walk-around inspection per IATA AHM 913
l4_steps.input: IATA AHM 913 inspection checklist, equipment logbook from prior shift
l4_steps.output: Completed pre-use inspection record; pass/fail status logged in Ramco
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-use inspection completion rate 100%; open defects from prior shift actioned before use
l4_steps.pain_point: Inspection checklist compliance drops during early-morning wave peaks; IATA AHM 913 requires 100% completion but enforcement is manual and shift-dependent

l4_steps.name: Validate GPU/ACU electrical output and hose integrity
l4_steps.input: Pre-use inspection pass record, GPU/ACU test equipment readings
l4_steps.output: Voltage/frequency validation report; unit cleared or grounded
l4_steps.kpi: GPU/ACU pre-use pass rate ≥98%; voltage within ±2% of 115V AC / 400 Hz spec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aging GPU units exhibit voltage fluctuations not detected by manual test protocols; risk of avionics damage if aircraft switched from APU to non-compliant ground power

l4_steps.name: Connect GPU and switch aircraft to ground power on block-in
l4_steps.input: Block-in confirmation from AMS, GPU readiness status
l4_steps.output: Aircraft on external ground power; APU shutdown initiated by flight crew
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft on ground power within 3 min of block-in; APU shutdown compliance ≥90% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground power connection delays extend APU run time; each additional minute of APU operation costs ~$12–15 in fuel and increases CO₂ emissions beyond CORSIA allowances

l4_steps.name: Deploy belt loaders and baggage tractors for cargo transfer
l4_steps.input: ULD/baggage load plan from departure control system, belt loader assignment
l4_steps.output: Belt loaders and tractors positioned and operational at aircraft doors
l4_steps.kpi: Belt loader/tractor on-stand on-time rate ≥95%; FOD incidents attributable to GSE ≤0 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Belt loader height mis-calibration causes FOD risk and potential cargo damage; no automated alignment verification in SITA AMS — relies on ramp agent visual check

l4_steps.name: Position fueling equipment and coordinate refueling start
l4_steps.input: Fuel uplift order from flight dispatch, fueling equipment availability status
l4_steps.output: Fuel truck or hydrant dispenser positioned; refueling sequence initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Fueling equipment on-stand within 10 min of block-in; fueling completion ≥15 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Fueling equipment scheduling not integrated with AMS turnaround timer; manual coordination via radio introduces sequencing delays that cascade to departure time

l4_steps.name: Log GSE defect in maintenance system with fault code
l4_steps.input: Observed defect during or after turnaround, equipment ID and location
l4_steps.output: Defect record with fault code, severity, and timestamp in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Defect logged within 15 min of identification; compliance ≥98%; zero unlogged defects on end-of-day fleet check
l4_steps.pain_point: Field staff reluctant to log minor defects fearing shift-end paperwork burden; systematic under-reporting creates hidden fleet degradation trends undetected until failure

l4_steps.name: Assess safety criticality and ground unit if required
l4_steps.input: Defect record, safety-criticality matrix (airline-proprietary), regulatory requirements
l4_steps.output: Safety classification (critical / non-critical); out-of-service tag issued for critical units
l4_steps.kpi: Safety-critical GSE grounded within 30 min of defect identification; zero safety-critical units operated beyond grounding threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: No standardised IATA or ICAO safety-criticality matrix for GSE defects; airlines use proprietary criteria, creating inconsistency during auditor spot-checks and insurance reviews

l4_steps.name: Execute corrective maintenance and post-repair check
l4_steps.input: Work order from AMOS, spare parts from stores, OEM repair manual
l4_steps.output: Repaired GSE unit with completed work order; post-repair serviceability test result
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective maintenance turnaround time ≤4 hr for critical GSE; ≤24 hr for non-critical; first-time fix rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Spare parts availability for aging diesel GSE (10+ yr pushback tugs, belt loaders) declining as OEMs shift to electric-only product lines; repair lead times increasing 30–60 days

l4_steps.name: Update GSE fleet availability status in AMS
l4_steps.input: Work order closure in AMOS, post-repair serviceability confirmation
l4_steps.output: GSE unit status updated to 'Serviceable' in AMS fleet registry
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet availability status updated within 1 hr of repair closure; AMS–AMOS sync accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS availability flags not automatically synced from AMOS work order closure; manual dual-entry required, introducing status lag and risk of re-assigning grounded units

l4_steps.name: Compile monthly GSE utilisation and MTBF KPIs
l4_steps.input: AMOS maintenance history, AMS utilisation logs, defect register extract
l4_steps.output: Monthly GSE performance dashboard: MTBF, downtime rate, utilisation by equipment class
l4_steps.kpi: GSE MTBF ≥500 operating hr; fleet downtime rate ≤3%; dashboard published by 5th of each month
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE telematics data not consistently ingested into Tableau; units lacking IoT sensors require manual log extraction, creating fleet visibility gaps in the monthly KPI pack

l4_steps.name: Assess fleet adequacy and identify replacement candidates
l4_steps.input: GSE performance dashboard, asset age register, peak-demand utilisation ratios
l4_steps.output: Fleet adequacy assessment; list of assets recommended for replacement or disposal
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet adequacy ratio ≥1.2× peak demand; assets beyond 10-yr economic life flagged for replacement within next budget cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Capital expenditure approval for GSE replacement requires 12–18 month lead time via SAP Ariba; aging fleet regularly operates beyond economic life, increasing failure risk and MRO cost

l4_steps.name: Initiate GSE procurement or lease request via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Approved fleet replacement list, capital budget allocation, airport authority concession terms
l4_steps.output: Purchase requisition or lease agreement raised in SAP Ariba; vendor shortlist for tender
l4_steps.kpi: Procurement lead time ≤90 days for standard GSE; ≤180 days for electric/specialist units
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport authority GSE concession agreements at certain airports restrict airline-owned equipment, requiring third-party GSE sourcing at higher cost and lower operational control
